Quick Help

How to Use iEnvi Field Data Tool

  1. Step 1: Set/lock the Project ID, enter your name.
  2. Step 2: Set location — tap the GPS button or click directly on the map.
  3. Step 3: Start recording — click a map location to choose a record type (Site, Soil, Water, Gas).
  4. Step 4: Fill in the form details and click Save.
  5. Step 5: Use bottom action buttons:
    • Add current sample (green) - Continue at same location
    • Complete site visit (blue) - Finish and export data
  6. Mobile tip: Scroll past the map by swiping from the screen edge.
  7. Note: Daily Report and Safety buttons are always accessible in the action bar.

Status Indicators

📍 ±35m = GPS accuracy 🏗️ Site ID = Current site 💾 0 saved = Records count

These show your current GPS accuracy, locked Site ID, and number of records saved for the current site.

Basic Workflow

  1. Lock Project ID: Enter project name/date, tap the green Lock button
  2. Get Location: Tap the GPS button in the top bar
  3. Select Category: Choose Soil/Water/Gas/Site from category cards
  4. Fill Details: Complete the form that appears
  5. Save Record: Use blue Save button in top bar or green "Add current sample" button at bottom
  6. Complete Site: Use "Complete site visit" button (blue) at bottom when finished

Tip: All buttons are optimised for touch on mobile devices.

Voice Input

Tap any text field, then use the microphone button on your keyboard (🎤) for voice input. This works better than web speech, especially with gloves on.

Troubleshooting & Updates

  • Can't save? Check: Site ID locked ✓ GPS location set ✓ Category selected ✓
  • GPS not working? Enable location services in phone settings. Move to open area.
  • Map not loading? Check internet connection. Offline tiles must be pre-cached.
  • Mobile scrolling issues? Swipe from the screen edge to scroll past the map.
  • Lost work? The app auto-saves your draft every 30 seconds to browser storage.

iEnvi Field Tool – Standard Operating Procedure

Quick Reference – Updated Interface (v3.0)

Element Style/Function Details
All Buttons Glass-morphism design 44px height, 12px radius, consistent shadows
GPS (Green Glass) Get device location Top bar, green gradient (#10b981)
Save (Blue Glass) Save current record Top bar, blue gradient (#3b82f6)
Daily Report (Cyan Glass) Daily Field Report — site log, crew, weather, notes Top bar, cyan gradient (#06b6d4)
Safety (Orange Glass) Safety Plan / Risk Assessment Top bar, orange gradient (#f59e0b)
Background Lighter pastels Improved contrast, softer appearance
Mobile Map Side borders added 10px margins for easier scrolling

1. Purpose

Standardise field data collection for environmental site assessments with offline capability, GPS accuracy tracking, and quality assurance features.

2. Pre-Field Preparation

  1. Device Setup:
    • Charge device to 100%
    • Enable GPS/Location Services
    • Clear browser cache if experiencing issues
    • Test camera permissions
  2. App Setup:
    • Open tool in Chrome/Safari
    • Sign in to Google (if using Drive backup)
    • Pre-cache map tiles for site area while online
    • Create Site ID format: YYYYMMDD_Location

3. Field Workflow

A. Site Arrival

  1. Lock Project ID (e.g., "20250804 Gympie QLD")
  2. Get initial GPS fix – aim for ±10m or better
  3. Complete safety checklist if required

B. Data Collection

  1. Location: Tap GPS button, wait for best accuracy
  2. Category: Select appropriate type:
    • SOIL → Boreholes, test pits, surface samples
    • WATER → Monitoring wells, surface water
    • GAS → Gas monitoring, ambient readings
    • SITE → Features, structures, observations
  3. Details: Complete all relevant fields
  4. Photos: Tap PHOTO button, include scale reference
  5. Voice Notes: Use keyboard mic for descriptions
  6. Save: Tap SAVE button (auto-generates next ID)

C. Quality Checks

  • GPS accuracy ≤15m for critical locations
  • All mandatory fields completed
  • Photos clear and properly oriented
  • Sample IDs sequential and unique

4. Data Management

Action Method When
Auto-save Browser storage Every 5 seconds
Local backup Export JSON End of each day
Cloud backup Google Drive When online
Final export CSV/Sheets Project completion

5. Sample ID Convention

Type Prefix Example
BoreholeBHBH01, BH02
Test PitTPTP01, TP02
Surface SampleSSSS01, SS02
Monitoring WellMWMW01, MW02
Surface WaterSWSW01, SW02
Gas MonitorGMGM01, GM02
QA DuplicateQ_QS01, QW01

6. Troubleshooting Guide (Updated)

Issue Solution
GPS won't lock Move to open area, wait 30s, check phone settings
Can't save record Check: Site ID locked? GPS set? Category selected?
Map scrolling difficult Use the side borders (10px margins) to scroll past map on mobile
Buttons too small All buttons now 44px height with improved touch targets
Poor contrast Background colors lightened to pastels for better visibility
Map tiles missing Pre-cache when online, or work without map
App crashes Clear browser cache, restart, data auto-saved
Export fails Check internet, try JSON export as backup

7. Best Practices & UI Tips

  • 🔋 Start with full battery, bring power bank
  • 📍 Always verify GPS accuracy before saving
  • 📸 Include scale reference in photos
  • 🎤 Use voice input for detailed descriptions
  • 💾 Export backup at lunch and end of day
  • ✅ Review all records before leaving site
  • 🌐 Sync to cloud as soon as online

New Interface Features:

  • • Glass buttons: All buttons have consistent glass-morphism styling
  • • Mobile optimization: Map has side borders for easier scrolling
  • • Better contrast: Lighter background gradients improve readability
  • • Touch targets: 44px minimum button height for gloved hands
  • • Visual consistency: 12px border radius throughout interface

Google Maps key

Address search, suggestions, and hospital lookup use one browser key. Paste the rotated key once. It is saved only in this browser under iEnvi_Config (localStorage field GOOGLE_API_KEY), not in the GitHub repo. The key is still visible to this page after that, so the real protection is an HTTP referrer restriction in Google Cloud for https://mikesbdj.github.io/*.

Risk Matrix Reference

Likelihood: 1=Rare, 2=Unlikely, 3=Possible, 4=Likely, 5=Almost Certain
Consequence: 1=Insignificant, 2=Minor, 3=Moderate, 4=Major, 5=Catastrophic

Stop Work Conditions

Any worker must stop work immediately if any of these conditions occur. Work only resumes when the issue is resolved and it is safe to continue.

🛑 Unsafe conditions observed
⛈️ Adverse weather (lightning, high winds, extreme heat)
🔧 Equipment failure or defect
😓 Worker fatigue or illness
📋 Significant change in scope or conditions
🎓 Lack of competency for task
